text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired (PD-88123) — service=open-inference — symptom=latency.p99 > 1200ms, p95 trending high. Link: https://pagerduty.company/PD-88123

maria: acked on PD, I'm taking lead. triage starting. :wave:
devon: on it — looking at graphs now, eu-west shows p95 jump at 12:03 UTC
eli: also seeing a rise in KV cache evictions and sidecar CPU on the affected pods
maria: ok devon/eli — can one of you grab recent sidecar logs and post any eviction/oom lines? run `kubectl logs -n inference sidecar-*-eu-west --since=5m`
devon: pasted logs: ```stderr
I kvcache: evicting 128 entries due to mem_pressure
W sidecar: cache_miss spike for model=open-1.3 at seq_len=1024
E runtime: slow decode loop > 500ms
```

eli: stack traces look like repeated tokenizer cold starts too. tail latency correlates with many small requests that miss the shared KV prefix cache
maria: that fits — customer traffic profile changed after a release spike, autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough
tara: noticed autoscaler events: `HPA scaled up from 2 -> 3 at 12:05, failed to reach target due to pod image pull backoff on one node`

maria: ugh image pullbackoff on warmup nodes explains sluggish capacity ramp. can infra confirm node pool health? @sre-rotation any regen in progress?
sre-rotation: checking node pool - one node in eu-west had docker overlay kernel panic and got cordoned at 12:04, we have limited spare capacity
devon: for immediate mitigation i can: 1) increase autoscaler minReplicas to 5, 2) enable temporary traffic diversion to fallback-model (quantized), 3) bump KV cache retention TTLs
maria: do it. prefer minimal blast radius: divest small % (10-20%) traffic to fallback-model first. add metrics alert for error-rate after diversion
devon: `kubectl patch hpa inference-hpa -n inference --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":5}]'` applied. verifying pods start.
eli: started warming new pods, but one pod stuck `ImagePullBackOff`. opening a quick infra ticket, assigning to infra oncall

maria: traffic diversion started: routed 15% to fallback-model via routing flag. Realtime dashboard: p99 dropped from ~1300ms -> ~420ms for the routed shard
tara: customer impacts — support flagged 3 SLO alerts from two enterprise tenants, they reported slow responses and one retry loop client behaviour

maria: internal note: impact = degraded latency for a subset of users (~12:03–12:25 UTC), retries observed, no traffic loss or errors beyond transient 503s on busiest routes
sre-rotation: infra quickfix: cordoned node replaced, kubelet restarted, image pull issue was transient registry throttling — pulling from mirror now
devon: new pods are Ready=4/5, traffic still diverted. p95 trending down but tail is choppy due to cold tokenizers

eli: pushing a quick cache-priming patch: pre-warm top N hot prefixes after pod Ready. command: `curl -X POST https://console.internal/prewarm -d '{"prefixes": ["/hot/*"]}'` — applied to new instances
maria: good. add a short-lived admission rule to avoid routing tiny 1-token requests to the main hot path while cache is cold (route them to fallback)
tara: FYI i informed CS and sent a brief customer bulletin noting degraded latency and mitigation steps, asked for impacted customer list

devon: p99 now stabilized ~260ms, p95 ~90ms for main path, overall request rate steady. monitoring closely for next 30m

sre-rotation: handoff note — i'll take the follow-up rotation. maria, if you want a formal incident page we can elevate; otherwise we'll keep as priority-2 mitigation and close when stable for 30m
maria: prefer to keep as active until tomorrow morning postmortem and until we validate registry mirror + autoscaler hysteresis playbook. handing to @sre-rotation in 10m. thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-88123 acknowledged by maria and resolved automatically after final confirmation — status=stable, timeline: 12:03–12:22 UTC. Follow-up: postmortem and registry mirror + autoscaler hysteresis playbook.
